R-ATTRIBUTION-001.text: A hit H is credited to opening O iff all three hold: - at H's entry event (PY_START or PY_RESUME), O's anchor is registered and is met on H's `f_back` chain before the first frame that either has its `f_code` in the cut `_CUT` (every `Handle._run` and `BaseEventLoop._run_once` code seen) or is the anchor of a registered opening whose `loop` is not the thread's running asyncio loop; the running loop is `O.loop` (the *loop boundary*); and no other registered opening of O's tracer is met there (revision 9, GAP-12: revision 8's sentence did not say that a foreign-loop anchor ends the walk, which M6's walk does; M6 is the rule, and this sentence now states it); - H then *confirms*, meaning its frame returns, yields, or unwinds at an offset other than its entry offset; - at that confirmation, O's tracer is still crediting (`id(M_T) in core.by_code`).
R-ATTRIBUTION-001.note: the attribution rule: each clause's mutant row

R-ATTRIBUTION-002.text: The anchor is the frame of the module-level `_run(core, …)` call, or the `_run_async` coroutine frame, that opened O.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-001.text: **Threat.** An exception can land at any bytecode of the machinery.
R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-001.note: the threat model; G_FI sweeps every bytecode

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-002.text: That includes a function's entry (RESUME) and a loop back-edge.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-003.text: On 3.13, an exception at a back-edge escapes the enclosing `try` table without running `finally` or a with-block's exit (CPython #130279; round-4 found-after item).

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-006.text: It also includes the machinery's own callbacks: a sys.monitoring callback is Python code with eval-breaker checks.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-007.text: **Sources:** signal-handler exceptions, KeyboardInterrupt, RecursionError, MemoryError, audit hooks, and a foreign tool raising at an event of one of our frames.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-008.text: That foreign tool can be a lower-id monitoring tool, or a settrace/setprofile function on the thread.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-013.text: (revision 8 self-audit, W2) `sys._getframe` in `_run` and `_run_async`, the argument of `_open` (M7), at every open;

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-018.text: `gc.get_referrers` in E2's sharing scan and in CLONE_ALIVE;

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-020.text: A hook that raises there cuts the registration short (M7, "The registration") and propagates out of the transaction (M5's heading).

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-039.text: (a) at F's entry event, O's anchor was registered and met on F's live chain before the cut, the running loop was `O.loop`, O.core held F's mint, and `id(M_T)` was in `O.core.by_code`;

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-040.text: (b) F then returned, yielded, or unwound at an offset other than its entry offset;

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-041.text: (c) at publication, `id(M_T)` was still in `O.core.by_code`, which exit empties in its first store after the claim.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-057.text: The mutex owner runs user code inside its transaction that waits for a thread, and that thread is itself waiting for the mutex.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-059.text: The waiter's bound breaks the cycle.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-060.text: After 10 s it raises MACHINERY_BUSY, its `with` releases the lock, and the owner proceeds (over-blocking #20).

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-070.text: A fault never causes any of these: over-credit; a hang; a mint left installed after the next reconciliation, unless its holder is a live zombie (L-ZOMBIE); or a poisoned later trace.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-071.text: A fault never swallows an exception, with one exception.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-082.text: Between E4 and E5: the same.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-083.text: At the facade's return, after E5: a zombie.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-086.text: `record()` refuses TRACE_ACTIVE, and `__exit__` again completes it.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-093.text: After the append, before the `try` (the rest of `_open`, and `_run` up to its `try`): an unregistered, inert opening that exit finalises as `"open"`.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-103.text: Before the claim: exit claims it as `("open", OPEN_AT_EXIT)`.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-104.text: After the claim: the cleanups are redone.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-105.text: `_run_async`'s `finally` skipped (a signal at the `await`'s throw-path back-edge on 3.12; M7): the same as "before the claim".

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-117.text: A fault loses at most that one credit and can never add one: an entry killed before its store has no pending entry, and a pending entry killed at its entry offset never publishes.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-118.text: A pending entry whose confirmation never arrives stays until `_retire` clears it.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-119.text: It keeps its frame, and that frame's callers, alive until then (L-MONITOR).

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-121.text: A second fault inside them is repaired by the next transaction.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-128.text: A `_register` exchange lands on another tool's id when an audit hook on `sys.monitoring.register_callback`, running inside that call before its exchange, lets another tool take the id; at most one exchange per registration does so, and the registration reports it (M7, "The registration").

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-133.text: A `free_tool_id` landing between `_ours()` and `set_events` made that call raise ValueError out of `run()` or its close.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-134.text: A free *and re-take* by another tool in that window made the call succeed on the foreign id.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-143.text: **L-ZOMBIE.** A tracer whose exit never began stays active.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-144.text: Causes: an exception at `__exit__`'s entry; a foreign tool raising at `__enter__`'s return event; or a harness's own `with` body ending in a loop on 3.13, where CPython #130279 skips `__exit__`.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-146.text: What persists: its equal-code mints stay installed, with their local events.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-149.text: That covers the common case: the fault that made it a zombie happened after the harness's `cov.run` calls returned.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-150.text: How long: until `__exit__()` is called, or until the facade becomes unreachable and some later enter or exit in the process reconciles.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-152.text: If a second fault leaves a stale anchor, the anchor frame's `f_back` chain can keep the facade reachable.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-154.text: Exceptions surfacing inside styxx callbacks take effect at that event.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-155.text: **Re-entry.** A finalizer, audit hook or signal handler that enters or exits a tracer inside another enter or exit on the same thread gets REENTRANT.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-156.text: In a finalizer this is printed as "Exception ignored" and that tracer fails.

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-171.text: a `run_async` section opened on the same thread inside the window and left suspended;

R-EXCEPTION_SAFETY_MODEL-172.text: a greenlet switch inside the window.

R-REASON_CODES-011.text: code: INSTANCE_PATH | status: changed | when it fires: entry: a module after the colon; a step whose own dict is missing, lacks the name, or is served by a Python-level `__dict__` descriptor (never called) | effect: raise

R-REASON_CODES-012.text: code: NOT_A_FUNCTION | status: changed | when it fires: entry: not FunctionType, staticmethod/classmethod of one, or an admissible C cache wrapper. **Also:** a cache wrapper whose real callee is not its own-dict `__wrapped__`; whose callee is bound by name in the module or holder; with a sibling cache wrapper of the same callee there; two different declared objects reaching one F_T | effect: raise; the message names the remedy (`declare <name>` or `'<module>:<name>.__wrapped__'`)

R-REASON_CODES-013.text: code: RESERVED_TARGET | status: **new** | when it fires: entry: F_T is `Handle._run` or `BaseEventLoop._run_once`, or F_T's code is a cut code | effect: raise

R-REASON_CODES-016.text: code: REENTRANT | status: **new** | when it fires: enter or exit re-entered on the same thread from inside a transition (a finalizer, audit hook or signal handler) | effect: enter: raise. Exit: recorded

R-REASON_CODES-017.text: code: MACHINERY_BUSY | status: **new** | when it fires: another thread held the machinery (the robust mutex) for more than 10 s. Revision 5: an open never waits, so it never raises this. Revision 4's open-side case is deleted | effect: enter: raise. Exit: recorded

R-REASON_CODES-021.text: code: NESTED_SECTION | status: changed (text) | when it fires: open: a registered opening of the same tracer is on the opener's chain before the cut (including an eager child's first step) | effect: raise + recorded

R-REASON_CODES-023.text: code: CLONE_ALIVE | status: changed | when it fires: exit: an unexplained reference to M_T and either (a) gc finds another FunctionType holding it, or (b) the gc freeze count *rose* since the mint was made and references remain that visible referrers do not explain | effect: recorded

R-REASON_CODES-024.text: code: CUT_MOVED | status: **new** | when it fires: at an entry event of minted code, or at exit: `Handle._run` or `BaseEventLoop._run_once` is not a function whose code is in the cut | effect: recorded at exit

R-REASON_CODES-025.text: code: TRACE_ACTIVE | status: changed (text) | when it fires: `record()` on a tracer that was never entered (its own text), inside its with-block, or a zombie | effect: raise

R-REASON_CODES-026.text: code: TRACE_INCOMPLETE | status: changed | when it fires: `record()` after an exit that began but did not finish; after a failed enter; or in a process other than the one that entered it | effect: raise

R-REASON_CODES-029.text: code: BAD_TRACE | status: changed | when it fires: score: any schema clause fails, with the exact type tested before any hash or compare (`end`, `gates_sha256`, keys, codes); unknown or retired note or problem codes | effect: refuse

R-REASON_CODES-033.text: code: NOT_EXERCISED | status: changed (text) | when it fires: score: a declared target is missing from the union of its section's `calls` | effect: refuse

R-REASON_CODES-034.text: code: note OPEN_AT_EXIT | status: changed | when it fires: exit: the opening was still open; also "pruned: the trace's own exit did not run" | effect: never refuses

R-REASON_CODES-035.text: code: note LAZY_RESULT | status: changed | when it fires: `run()` got an exact generator, coroutine or async generator back; new text; "(its body had not started)" when unstarted | effect: never refuses
